SL-000019.transcript:
Member (Liam Campbell): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Liam Campbell, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Campbell): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Liam Campbell): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Liam Campbell): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): How old is he?
Member (Liam Campbell): Fourteen.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Liam Campbell): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Liam Campbell): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Liam Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Liam Campbell): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Liam Campbell): Great, that helps.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Liam Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000019.narrative_summary: Liam Campbell, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a coverage question case. Agent Daniel Okafor checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 5 (very satisfied).

SL-000085.transcript:
Member (Fatima Ahmed): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Fatima Ahmed, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Yes, that's right.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Fatima Ahmed): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Fatima Ahmed): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Fatima Ahmed): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Singh): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Owen Singh, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Singh): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Owen Singh): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Owen Singh): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.

Member (Owen Singh): So I'm still waiting with no income?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.

Member (Olivia Kim): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.

Member (Hannah Cote): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Hannah Cote, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.

Member (Emma Campbell): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Emma Campbell, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.

Member (Emma Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Campbell): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Emma Campbell): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Emma Campbell): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Emma Campbell): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Emma Campbell): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Emma Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Emma Campbell): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Emma Campbell): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Emma Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Hannah Morrison, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.

Member (Hannah Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Hannah Morrison): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Hannah Morrison): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Which pharmacy are you using?

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?

Member (Hannah Morrison): How long does the review take once it's in?

Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.

SL-000868.transcript:
Member (Arjun Patel): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Arjun Patel, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Patel): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun Patel): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Arjun Patel): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Arjun Patel): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Arjun Patel): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Arjun Patel): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Arjun Patel): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with your previous paid claims and the plan booklet.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Arjun Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Arjun Patel): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Arjun Patel): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Arjun Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Mei Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Mei Chen): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.

Member (Mei Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Member (Liam Fortin): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Liam Fortin): Can I appeal it?

Member (Liam Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Member (Lucas Kim): The orthodontist wants to start next month.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Lucas Kim): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Lucas Kim): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Lucas Kim): Great, that helps.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.

Member (Emma Roy): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Emma Roy, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): When did you go off work?

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Emma Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Emma Roy): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Emma Roy): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Emma Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Member (Arjun Wilson): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.

Member (Arjun Wilson): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Arjun Wilson): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.

Member (Noah Lavoie): I'm following up again — I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.

Member (Noah Lavoie): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Noah Lavoie): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Lavoie): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah Lavoie): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Where is the money going?
Member (Noah Lavoie): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Noah Lavoie): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Noah Lavoie): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Noah Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Noah Lavoie): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Noah Lavoie): Who follows up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Noah Lavoie): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
